section_summary: These pages trace 1948 efforts to reopen Japanese patent registration and restore foreign industrial property rights lost during the war. They include SCAP directives, correspondence with American firms and the National Foreign Trade Council, and a detailed Swiss request to license DDT manufacture in Japan. The section ends with discussion of patent policy before the Far Eastern Commission.

subfiles.title: Proposal to restore cancelled American patents and trademarks
subfiles.from: Stephen P. Ladas, Langner, Parry, Card & Langner
subfiles.about: Proposes repealing Japan’s wartime industrial property law and preserving rights that lapsed during the war.
subfiles.summary: Ladas urges automatic restoration of cancelled United Nations nationals’ patents and trademarks, rather than individual applications, and exclusion of the war period from renewal and other deadlines.

subfiles.title: Reply to Stephen P. Ladas on restoration of industrial property
subfiles.about: Explains the proposed international program for restoring foreign patent and trademark rights in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Vernon distinguishes the property memorandum from industrial property policy and says a restoration program awaits Far Eastern Commission approval. It would revalidate patents, address royalties or term extensions, and extend priority periods; technical reasons may require owners to apply.

subfiles.title: Suspension of SCAPIN 1923 concerning trademarks
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports suspension of a SCAP trademark order after a Westinghouse complaint.
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 1923, concerning use of former holding company and monopoly marks, was suspended for further study. Westinghouse warned that weakening the Mitsubishi mark could harm Mitsubishi Pencil, which used it independently.

subfiles.title: Request for Japanese patents meeting
subfiles.about: Asks whether a Japanese patents meeting can be arranged for Bradley on September 24.
subfiles.summary: Loree requests a Friday appointment for Bradley.

subfiles.title: Japanese patents meeting appointment
subfiles.about: Sets a meeting on Japanese patents for September 24.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman arranges an 11 a.m. meeting and requests confirmation through Lewis.

subfiles.title: Request for copies of SCAP patent documents
subfiles.about: Asks whether recent SCAP patent directive and explanatory documents will be available at the meeting.
subfiles.summary: Behr requests copies of the directive, statement, and Civil Property Custodian memorandum.

subfiles.title: Japanese registration of foreign patents
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAPIN 5981-A and a press release on foreign patent applications.
subfiles.summary: The despatch explains that foreign filings are now permitted, while patent licensing remains prohibited.

subfiles.title: Registration of Patent Properties, SCAPIN 5981-A
subfiles.from: R. M. Levy, for the Supreme Commander
subfiles.about: Authorizes foreign patent, utility model, and design applications and directs repeal of wartime restrictions.
subfiles.summary: SCAP rescinds earlier restrictions and directs repeal of specified Wartime Law articles.

subfiles.title: To Accept Foreign Applications for Patent Rights
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Far East Command, Public Information Office
subfiles.about: Announces the reopening of Japanese patent applications to foreign applicants.
subfiles.summary: The release describes registration, mailing of specifications, and twelve-month convention priority. It clarifies that older published foreign patents remain subject to existing Japanese law.

subfiles.title: Inquiry on Japanese patent applications
subfiles.from: R. W. Gannon, American Chemical Paint Company
subfiles.about: Seeks confirmation of foreign filing rules and guidance on protecting wartime inventions.
subfiles.summary: Gannon asks about priority limits, published patents, and application channels.

subfiles.title: Reply to American Chemical Paint Company
subfiles.about: Explains current filing rules and proposed restoration measures.
subfiles.summary: Vernon confirms that foreigners may apply, explains current priority and publication limits, and anticipates later relief under a program awaiting Far Eastern Commission approval. He promises further information on filing channels.

subfiles.title: Industrial property situation in Japan
subfiles.from: Robert F. Loree, National Foreign Trade Council
subfiles.about: Urges faster SCAP action on the Council’s industrial property recommendations.
subfiles.summary: Loree submits the Council’s recommendations and argues that unresolved issues could delay American industry’s return to Japan.

subfiles.title: Japanese Patents, Trademarks and Marks of Origin
subfiles.from: National Foreign Trade Council Industrial Property Committee
subfiles.about: Sets out recommendations on patents, origin marking, and access to Japanese technical information.
subfiles.summary: The committee seeks extended terms and priority, reinstatement, tax relief, licensing rights, and changes to Japanese patent law. It also urges strict export marking and opposes broad copying of Japanese technical information.

subfiles.title: Routing memorandum on Council letter
subfiles.about: Requests a reply to Loree’s October 13 letter.
subfiles.summary: Lewis asks for a substantive or interim reply for Saltzman’s signature.

subfiles.title: Reply to Robert F. Loree
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Council recommendations and anticipates a Far Eastern Commission decision.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman thanks Loree and expects a decision on United States patent policy proposals soon.

subfiles.title: Draft reply to Robert F. Loree
subfiles.about: Explains why SCAP action would await Far Eastern Commission policy approval.
subfiles.summary: An earlier draft cites international commitments requiring a Commission decision before occupation authorities act.

subfiles.title: Japanese Patents, Trademarks and Marks of Origin: Progress Report
subfiles.from: National Foreign Trade Council Industrial Property Committee
subfiles.about: Reports the committee’s proposals, SCAP’s initial action, and other industrial property concerns.
subfiles.summary: The bulletin lists recommendations on patent restoration, terms, taxes, licensing, and Japanese law. It says the September directive addresses only part of the program and discusses country of origin markings and access to technical information.

subfiles.title: The Wartime Law of Industrial Property
subfiles.about: Reproduces provisions restricting enemy-owned industrial property during wartime.
subfiles.summary: The law provides for suspended applications, cancellation, exclusive use, and penalties.

subfiles.title: Registration of Patent Properties, SCAPIN 5981-A
subfiles.from: R. M. Levy, for the Supreme Commander
subfiles.about: Reproduces the directive allowing foreign patent applications and repealing wartime restrictions.
subfiles.summary: SCAP authorizes foreign filings and directs repeal of five Wartime Law articles.

subfiles.title: Applications Accepted Here for Foreign Patent Rights
subfiles.about: Explains the new foreign filing rules and their twelve-month priority limit.
subfiles.summary: The statement announces foreign filings and explains continuing limits for older applications and published patents.

subfiles.title: NFTC Memorandum on Comments by SCAP Relative to Japanese Patents
subfiles.about: Responds point by point to SCAP comments on patent reform and related recommendations.
subfiles.summary: The Council argues that term extensions should include surviving patents and opposes compulsory licensing, criminal penalties, opposition proceedings, annual fees, and working requirements. It also seeks origin markings on all Japanese exports and tighter limits on access to technical information.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about patent and trademark filings
subfiles.about: Asks whether applications may be filed in Japan and requests the SCAP directive.
subfiles.summary: Rivise requests filing guidance and a copy of the new directive.

subfiles.title: Reply to C. W. Rivise
subfiles.about: Sends a press release concerning foreign applications for new trademarks.
subfiles.summary: Vernon encloses a recently received occupation press release.

subfiles.title: Swiss request for DDT patent licensing in Japan
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits Swiss correspondence seeking a DDT patent licensing agreement and royalties.
subfiles.summary: Sebald recounts J. R. Geigy’s requests, occupation refusals, and Japanese DDT production. He notes that foreign licensing remains prohibited despite renewed patent registration and urges a policy on use of foreign-owned patents and processes.

subfiles.title: Swiss Mission note submitting Geigy DDT documents
subfiles.about: Submits Geigy documents and requests favorable consideration of DDT licensing.
subfiles.summary: The Mission forwards Britt’s letter, memorandum, draft agreement, and patent text.

subfiles.title: Britt letter on Geigy DDT license
subfiles.to: SCAP Public Health and Welfare Section
subfiles.about: Requests steps toward approval of a Geigy DDT patent license.
subfiles.summary: Britt sends a memorandum and draft agreement for review.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Geigy Japanese DDT Patent No. 169665
subfiles.to: SCAP Public Health and Welfare Section
subfiles.about: Asserts infringement and proposes licensing terms for Japanese DDT manufacture.
subfiles.summary: Britt describes Japanese production and Geigy’s patent claim. He seeks licenses, retroactive five-percent royalties, transfer of proceeds to Switzerland, and inspection rights through the patent’s term.

subfiles.title: Draft Patent License Agreement for DDT Insecticides
subfiles.about: Sets proposed terms for Japanese domestic manufacture and sale of DDT insecticides.
subfiles.summary: The draft provides for a nonexclusive license, five-percent royalties including past sales, records and inspections, limits on exports and trademarks, and arbitration.

subfiles.title: SCAP response to Swiss DDT licensing request
subfiles.about: Declines to approve the proposed DDT license under current Allied directives.
subfiles.summary: SCAP says it lacks authority and returns the submitted enclosures.

subfiles.title: Swiss request for reconsideration of DDT license
subfiles.about: Requests renewed consideration and DDT production figures.
subfiles.summary: The Mission forwards Britt’s new memorandum and seeks the requested statistics.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Geigy Patent Japan No. 169665
subfiles.about: Reasserts Geigy’s DDT patent claim and seeks import and production information.
subfiles.summary: Britt argues that Japanese manufacture using imported concentrate requires the patent owner’s consent and royalties. He requests quantities, values, distribution, and manufacture figures.

subfiles.title: SCAP memorandum supplying DDT figures
subfiles.about: Explains DDT procurement and distribution, provides figures, and defers licensing.
subfiles.summary: SCAP distinguishes military procurement before January 1947 from later Japanese Government responsibility and supplies DDT import and production figures. It states that policy still prohibits patent property transactions between persons inside and outside Japan, so licensing and royalties remain in abeyance.

subfiles.title: Authorization to approve FEC 284/6
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, Department of State
subfiles.to: United States Representative on the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Authorizes approval of the patent, utility model, and design policy paper.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman authorizes the United States vote for FEC 284/6.

subfiles.title: Japanese Production of Railroad Stokers
subfiles.about: Records Charles J. Surdy’s concerns about Japanese use of his company’s stoker designs.
subfiles.summary: Surdy seeks compensation and protection against competing exports. Vernon offers reasonable help with patent rights while explaining the Department’s objection to market divisions based on unpatented technology.

subfiles.title: Inquiry concerning decision on German patents
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Seeks identification of a decision on German patents mentioned in Far Eastern Commission proceedings.
subfiles.summary: Sebald asks whether the reference means the London Accord and requests relevant information for SCAP.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Commission Committee No. 1 meeting minutes
subfiles.about: Records debate on reparations and referral of Japanese patent policy proposals.
subfiles.summary: Members discuss sending patent proposals to a subcommittee; the United Kingdom member cites a German patent decision.
